title: SDK Dependency Refresh + Deprecated API Surface Purge
creator: Asha Patel
description: Consolidate and modernize the three client libraries (Python, JavaScript, Go) by bumping critical runtime and transport dependencies, removing deprecated API surface in the public SDKs, and performing performance-oriented cleanup (smaller bundles, fewer runtime transitive deps). This ticket covers dependency upgrades that unblock CI flakiness and a coordinated deprecation removal of legacy endpoints and client helpers that have been marked deprecated since 2025-Q4.
background: Over the last year we've accumulated drift across SDKs: multiple semver-pinned transitive dependencies causing CVE noise, inconsistent use of HTTP clients (requests vs. httpx in Python; node-fetch vs native fetch in JS), and a legacy API surface (v1/generate -> unified /responses API, old sync helpers) that complicates maintenance. These issues cause intermittent CI failures, larger shipping bundles for web customers, and make it hard to test new runtime features (streaming, function-calls) in a consistent way.
implementation_plan: Audit current direct + top-level transitive dependencies for each SDK and produce a matrix (target: minimal safe bumps)

Python: move from requests 2.x to requests 2.31+ (or optionally httpx for async flows) for consistency; upgrade protobuf/grpcio to versions compatible with runtime-1.22; pin typing extensions and bump packaging to latest

JavaScript/TS: replace node-fetch with native fetch where possible, bump ts-node/typescript and @types/node, ensure ESM/CJS compatibility for bundlers; reduce bundle size by switching to modular entrypoints
Go: update go.mod to use latest public client v2, bump dependencies (google/uuid, protobuf) and run `go vet`/`golangci-lint` fixes
Deprecation purge: remove legacy helpers (Client.generate(), old streaming shim) and delete shimmed endpoint routes in client code; add compile/runtime warnings for any remaining aliases
Add comprehensive compatibility test matrix in CI (python 3.10-3.12, node 18-20, go 1.20-1.22) and run full e2e against staging runtime-1.22
Publish migration guides and an automated codemod for major breaking changes (JS/TS recommended codemod), and set npm/pypi release notes to highlight breaking removals
Staged release: beta releases for each SDK (rc/beta) followed by GA after 2 weeks of usage and telemetry checks
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Dependency matrix completed. Identified two high-risk transitive libraries in JS bundling (legacy lodash builds) and a Python dependency causing intermittent SSL failures in some regions.
2026-02-28: Python PR opened to bump requests and packaging; tests failing on async path — investigating httpx fallback option.
2026-03-05: JS prototype branch replaced node-fetch with native fetch and introduced a small wrapper for older Node consumers. Bundle size reduced by ~12% in initial measurements.
2026-03-10: Go module updates committed; CI lint failures fixed. Added go 1.22 to the CI matrix.
2026-03-12: First beta packages published to test PyPI and npm with internal feature flags enabled. Observability shows no increase in error rates in staging.
testing_plan: Run unit suites and end-to-end tests against staging runtime-1.22 with full matrix. Add targeted fuzz tests for streaming and function-calling flows that previously had flaky failures. Include smoke tests for old-deprecated endpoints to ensure clients receive 410 responses with migration headers. Validate packaging by installing from the published beta artifacts in a clean environment for each language.
migration_notes: Publish a migration guide at docs.redwood.com/sdk-migration-2026 with: mapping of removed helpers to new calls, code snippets (Python/JS/Go), and a js codemod for the most common renames. For users unable to upgrade immediately, maintain a thin compatibility shim package (deprecated, receives only security fixes) for one release cycle; advertise end-of-life date in deprecation headers and console announcements.
rollback_plan: If beta telemetry shows regressions or high error rates, revert the SDK packages and re-enable the compatibility shims in the runtime to accept the legacy surface for an additional 30 days. In the worst case, publish a patched minor release that restores behavior and reopen the deprecation timeline.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Breaking changes in dependency API surface could cause subtle runtime differences (e.g., HTTP timeout behavior). Mitigation: add explicit integration tests for timeouts and retry semantics.
Risk: Bundle/tooling edge cases for ESM/CJS consumers. Mitigation: provide two published entrypoints and CI tests that install from npm in both ESM and CommonJS projects.

Risk: Unexpected customer CI failures after removal of deprecated helpers. Mitigation: staged rollout, deprecation headers, and compatibility shim with telemetry; provide live support for top customers.
Risk: Security CVEs in transitive deps. Mitigation: upgrade to fixed versions and run snyk/oss-audit as gate in CI.
estimated_impact: This cleanup is expected to reduce bundle sizes for web SDK consumers by ~10-15%, eliminate a recurring SSL/CI flakiness class for Python consumers, and remove a maintenance burden of legacy shims. It will also reduce security alert noise from transitive CVEs.
qa_checklist: All unit tests pass in CI for Python/JS/Go
E2E tests against staging runtime-1.22 pass
Beta packages install cleanly in minimal virtualenv and node projects
Codemod applied to sample repo and verified
Telemetry filters show no increase in 5xx rates after beta release
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs published as beta with changelogs and migration guides
No critical regressions observed in staging after 7 days of beta usage
Compatibility shim is available and documented for customers that cannot upgrade immediately
Deprecated API surface removed from main branches and associated docs updated
